questions.stem: (a) Define urbanisation. (b) State how large a city's population must be for it to be classed as a megacity.
markscheme: B1: urbanisation is the increasing percentage (proportion) of a country's population living in towns and cities
B1: a megacity has a population of more than 10 million people
questions.modelAnswer: (a) Urbanisation is the increasing percentage of a country's population living in towns and cities, driven by rural-urban migration and natural increase within cities. (b) A megacity is a city with a population of more than 10 million people, such as Tokyo, Delhi or Lagos.

questions.stem: For each factor below, state whether it is a push factor or a pull factor in migration: (a) drought destroying crops in the home region; (b) well-paid hospital jobs in the destination country.
markscheme: B1: (a) push factor — a negative condition that drives people away from the home region
B1: (b) pull factor — a positive attraction that draws people to the destination
questions.modelAnswer: (a) Drought destroying crops is a push factor: it is a negative condition (food shortage, lost income) that drives people away from the home region. (b) Well-paid hospital jobs are a pull factor: they are a positive attraction of the destination that draws people in. Most migration decisions involve a combination of both.

questions.stem: (a) On an Ordnance Survey map with a scale of 1:25 000, how many centimetres on the map represent 1 kilometre on the ground? (b) What name is given to the lines on a map that join points of equal height above sea level?
markscheme: B1: 4 cm (since 1 cm on the map represents 250 m on the ground)
B1: contour lines
questions.modelAnswer: (a) On a 1:25 000 map, 1 cm represents 25 000 cm, which is 250 m on the ground. A kilometre is 1 000 m, and 1 000 ÷ 250 = 4, so 4 cm on the map represents 1 km on the ground. (b) Lines joining points of equal height above sea level are contour lines; close contours show steep slopes and widely spaced contours show gentle slopes.

questions.stem: Explain how a waterfall forms and why it retreats upstream over time.
markscheme: B1: a layer of hard, resistant rock lies over softer rock, and the soft rock is eroded faster
B1: this undercutting leaves an unsupported overhang of hard rock above a plunge pool
B1: the overhang eventually collapses and the process repeats, so the waterfall retreats upstream leaving a steep-sided gorge
questions.modelAnswer: A waterfall forms where a layer of hard, resistant rock lies on top of softer rock. The soft rock is eroded faster by hydraulic action and abrasion, undercutting the hard layer and leaving an unsupported overhang, while eroded debris helps carve a plunge pool at the base. Eventually the overhang collapses under its own weight. As this cycle of undercutting and collapse repeats, the waterfall retreats upstream, leaving a steep-sided gorge behind it.

questions.stem: The same earthquake is felt in two fictional cities: Kestra reports Mercalli intensity VIII, while Lorm, 150 km away, reports intensity IV. Explain how one earthquake can have two different intensity values.
markscheme: B1: the Mercalli scale measures the observed effects and damage at each place, which vary with distance from the epicentre, ground type and building quality
B1: an earthquake has a single magnitude (energy released) but many different intensities
questions.modelAnswer: The Mercalli scale records the effects actually observed at each location — damage to buildings, how strongly people felt the shaking — and these depend on distance from the epicentre, the type of ground and building quality. Kestra, reporting VIII, was probably closer to the epicentre or had weaker buildings. An earthquake has just one magnitude (the energy released, e.g. on the Richter scale) but many different intensities, one for each place that experiences it.

questions.stem: The fictional company Vexa designs its smartphones in the country of Nordland, sources rare metals from mines in the country of Kabu, assembles the phones in the country of Saros, and sells them in shops on every continent. (a) What kind of company is Vexa? (b) Suggest TWO reasons why companies like Vexa spread their production across several countries.
markscheme: B1: Vexa is a transnational corporation (TNC) — a company operating in many countries
B1: first valid reason, e.g. lower labour costs / lower taxes / weaker regulation in the production country
B1: second, different valid reason, e.g. being close to raw materials (the mines) or close to markets, cutting costs
questions.modelAnswer: (a) Vexa is a transnational corporation (TNC): a large company that operates in many countries, splitting design, production and sales between them. (b) TNCs spread production to cut costs — for example, assembling in countries where wages, taxes or regulations are lower — and to be close to what they need, such as raw materials (Vexa's mines in Kabu) or major markets. Modern container shipping and instant communication make organising a chain like this cheap and easy.

questions.stem: The fictional city of Portan has doubled its population in twenty years. Describe TWO problems this rapid growth is likely to create, and for ONE of your problems, explain a sustainable solution.
markscheme: B1: first problem described, e.g. informal settlements of self-built housing lacking water, sanitation, electricity and secure tenure
B1: second, different problem, e.g. severe traffic congestion and air pollution / overstretched water, waste and health services
B1: a solution clearly linked to a named problem, e.g. upgrading settlements in place with sewers, standpipes and legal tenure (or bus rapid transit and cycle lanes for congestion)
questions.modelAnswer: First problem: housing — growth outpaces formal construction, so new arrivals build informal settlements of scrap materials, usually lacking clean water, sanitation, electricity and the legal right to stay. Second problem: congestion and pollution — roads built for far fewer people become gridlocked, and vehicle exhaust plus uncollected waste damage health. A sustainable solution for housing is to upgrade settlements in place rather than demolish them: paving roads, installing sewers and standpipes, and granting secure tenure lets residents improve their own homes without destroying their communities. (For congestion, a bus rapid transit system with dedicated lanes, as in Curitiba, would be an equally valid linked solution.)

questions.stem: The table shows development data for two fictional countries. Aldervale: GDP per capita ＄38 000; life expectancy 61 years; adult literacy rate 55%. Brescia: GDP per capita ＄12 000; life expectancy 79 years; adult literacy rate 98%. Which country is more developed overall? Use evidence from the table to justify your answer.
markscheme: B1: identifies Brescia as more developed overall
B1: evidence — Brescia's much higher life expectancy (79 years vs 61) shows better healthcare, nutrition and sanitation
B1: evidence — Brescia's much higher literacy rate (98% vs 55%) shows better education; GDP per capita alone is misleading because it hides quality of life and inequality
questions.modelAnswer: Brescia is more developed overall, despite its far lower GDP per capita. Its life expectancy of 79 years (against Aldervale's 61) shows its people have much better healthcare, nutrition and sanitation, and its literacy rate of 98% (against 55%) shows far wider access to education. Aldervale's high GDP per capita is misleading on its own: as an average, it could be inflated by a small wealthy elite, and it says nothing about health or education. This is exactly why the HDI combines income, life expectancy and schooling — Brescia would score far higher.
